messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P1: Possible cross-tenant KV cache exposure detected for customer HeliosHealth in vpc-dedicated pool-9. Please investigate. thread_ts=2004445678

Priya Rao: Ack. I'm the incident lead for this window. Kicking off investigation. What signals do we have?

Luis Chen: Pulling pool membership, router-proxy logs, and config-store history. Noted a rolling restart in pool-9 started ~2026-03-16T05:11Z.

Samir Patel: Looking at gateway logs: spikes in 500/502s at 05:12, and small number of 200s where payload metadata tenant_id != request tenant. Very low percentage (~0.05%) but must triage.

eng-runtime: Searching KV cache traces for tenant prefix collisions. Quick grep shows entries where the same key was resolved to different tenant_ids on different nodes around 05:12:14. Example: cache_get key=hh_user_82 -> tenant=helios, then same key -> tenant=solstice-pay.

Priya Rao: Ok, that suggests namespace mapping divergence. Any config-store diffs or snapshot mismatches?

Luis Chen: Config-store had concurrent commits: v305 at 05:08 and v308 at 05:10. One of the new router-proxy instances joined with a stale snapshot (v305) while control-plane advanced to v308. That instance's prefix mapping was older.

Samir Patel: To confirm exposure window I'm running a targeted scan: find all requests where cached metadata != origin metadata and collect counts + sanitized payloads. ETA ~4m.

eng-runtime: Evidence lines (sanitized):
```
05:12:14 cache_hit key=hh_user_82 -> returned_tenant=solstice-pay
05:12:14 origin_lookup key=hh_user_82 -> owner_tenant=helios
```

Priya Rao: Immediate containment: 1) drain suspect node(s) 2) pause autoscaling for pool-9 3) freeze config-store writes for prefix mappings 4) take forensic snapshots of cache memory. Eng-security join pls.

Luis Chen: Draining router-proxy-9c now, pausing scale group for pool-9. Commands:
```
# drain and stop
redwoodctl node drain --node router-proxy-9c --pool pool-9
redwoodctl node stop --node router-proxy-9c
# pause autoscale
redwoodctl pool autoscale --pool pool-9 --set disabled
```

eng-security: Oncall here. We'll coordinate EDR-friendly memory dump and record SHA256 hashes. No destructive ops until snapshots complete.

Ops-Runbook: Reminder: follow tenant-isolation runbook steps 2-5. Capture cache shards, network captures, and config-store state.

Samir Patel: Scan update: 78 requests identified in a 7-minute window (05:11:30-05:18:30) where cache returned a foreign-tenant value. Samples show no high-risk PII fields present in returned payloads but need full SRE+Security review.

Priya Rao: Good. eng-runtime, rotate cache namespace alias (append -v2) and invalidate relevant shards after snapshots. Luis, limit inter-pool routing until we have config hardening.

eng-runtime: Kicking cache alias rotation and TTL purge. Purge summary: ~9,450 keys evicted from pool-9 caches. Forcing config sync to v308 across pool-9.

Luis Chen: Applied iptables block between pool-9 and pool-4 subnets to prevent lateral reads while we reconcile.

eng-security: Snapshots completed, artifacts uploaded, hashes logged in SEC-2026-211. No evidence yet that origin datastore was written with wrong tenant. Copies stored in secure bucket with restricted ACL.

CSE - Marta: Preparing a short embargoed customer note for HeliosHealth: outline detection, immediate mitigations, and that a forensic audit is underway. Recommend we share now as a heads-up (no confirmed data leak).

Priya Rao: Agreed to send heads-up. Keep message factual and avoid speculation. Offer dedicated postmortem and remediation support.

Samir Patel: Post-mitigation metrics: error rate and mismatch counts returned to baseline within ~2m of draining and purge. No new mismatches after config sync.

eng-platform: Preliminary root cause: race in bootstrap where node falling back to local snapshot allowed older config to be used when config-store fetch timed out. Action: add strong pre-join config hash check and refuse to join if hashes differ. Will open PR and include unit/integration tests.

Priya Rao: Action owners (assign now):
- Incident lead: Priya Rao -> timeline + postmortem writeup
- Evidence & logs: Samir Patel (eng-runtime) -> full scan, sanitized samples uploaded to INC-2004445678-evidence
- Forensics: eng-security -> artifact analysis and chain-of-custody SEC-2026-211
- Platform changes: eng-platform -> PR for pre-join hash validation + deploy plan
- Customer comms: CSE - Marta -> HeliosHealth liaison + draft updates

Luis Chen: I'll keep autoscaling disabled for 45m then re-enable with strict canary. Will also add alert if new node boot with config version < current.

Priya Rao: Any objections to sending the brief to customer now?

CSE - Marta: Sending now. Subject: "Redwood Incident — transient cache namespace inconsistency affecting a small fraction of requests (HeliosHealth)". Including mitigations and next steps.

eng-security: Forensics report in progress. No confirmed persistence cross-tenant writes. Evidence suggests read-only cache divergence.

audit-bot: Forensic artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-sec/SEC-2026-211/ (sha256 sums recorded). Linked to incident INC-2004445678.

Priya Rao: Moving to monitoring + recovery. Incident P1 until forensics complete. Follow-ups: 1) postmortem within 72h 2) platform fix and release 3) customer readout. Handing overnight watch to Luis. Thanks team. :shield:
